steps.title: What we'll do today
steps.html:
You'll sign up for the free AI Claude and have your first conversation: ask a question, follow up, and hand it a long text to summarize.

  • Time: 10–15 minutes
  • Cost: free
  • You need: a phone or a computer, internet, and an email address (or a Google account)
Doing this on a phone? — You'll switch back and forth between this page (in your web browser) and the Claude app. To come back, just open the browser app that shows this page. Your progress is saved.

Don't worry about unfamiliar words. We explain each one the first time it comes up.

faq.a: A computer program that reads text and writes answers, a bit like a person. You can ask it questions or ask it to summarize and tidy up text.
Yes. Claude has a free plan. There's a daily limit, so if you use it a lot you may need to wait a while. If you don't enter payment details, you won't be charged.

steps.title: Where would you like to try it?
steps.html: You can pick the device you're reading this on, or a different one.

choices.label: Computer
choices.sub: Use it in a web browser

phone.title: Install the Claude app and sign up
phone.html:
1. Open your phone's app store.
    · iPhone: App Store (blue with an A)
    · Other phones: Play Store (colorful triangle)
  2. Tap Search and type Claude.
  3. Make sure the maker is Anthropic. There are other apps with similar names.
  4. Tap Get or Install, and when it's done, Open.
  5. Tap Continue with Google, or sign up with your email address. With email, enter the confirmation link (or code) sent to your inbox.

pc.title: Sign up for Claude
pc.html:
First open a browser, the program you use to look at the internet. Click Microsoft Edge (blue wave), Chrome (red, yellow and green circle), or on a Mac Safari (compass) at the bottom of your screen.

  1. Click the address bar at the very top, type claude.ai and press Enter.
  2. Click Continue with Google, or sign up with your email address.
  3. If you used email, click the button (or enter the code) in the confirmation email.

check.q: Did you finish signing up, and do you see a screen with a box to type in?

faq.q: It asks me to upgrade to a paid plan.
faq.a: Free is plenty. Tap Continue for free, Later, or ✕ to move on. If you don't enter payment details, you won't be charged.

faq.q: It asks for my age or phone number.
faq.a: That's part of the sign-up check. Enter your date of birth, and if it asks for a phone number, enter it and type in the code sent by text message.

steps.title: If signing up doesn't work
steps.html:
• If the confirmation email doesn't arrive, check your spam folder.
  • If you have a Google account, Continue with Google is the easiest.
  • If it asks for your country, pick the one you live in.
  • Can't find the app? Open claude.ai in your phone's web browser. It works the same way.

steps.title: Before you start — never type these in
steps.html:
What you write to an AI is sent to the company's servers. So it's best not to enter:

  • ID numbers, card numbers, passwords
  • Other people's personal details (name + phone number, etc.)
  • Confidential work documents
AI can be wrong, too — it sometimes gives answers that sound right but aren't. For important things like money, health or law, always double-check.

steps.title: Send your first question

phone.html:
At the bottom of the Claude app there's a box to type in. Tap it and the keyboard comes up.

  1. Press Copy on the box below.
  2. Go to the Claude app, press and hold the typing box, then tap Paste. (Typing it is fine too.)
  3. Tap the up arrow (↑) button to the right of the box to send.

pc.html:
In the middle (or bottom) of the Claude screen there's a box to type in.

  1. Press Copy on the box below.
  2. Click the typing box in Claude once and paste with Ctrl+V (⌘ command+V on a Mac). (Typing it is fine too.)
  3. Press Enter or click the up arrow (↑) button to send.

steps.code: I have eggs, tofu and kimchi in the fridge. Suggest just 3 dinner ideas for tonight.

check.q: Did Claude suggest some dinner ideas?

steps.title: If no answer comes
steps.html:
• Make sure you tapped the send button (↑). If the text is still in the box, it hasn't been sent yet.
  • The answer may appear slowly, word by word. Wait a few seconds.
  • If you see something like "usage limit", you've used up the free amount. Try again in a few hours.
  • Also check that your internet (Wi-Fi or data) is on.

steps.title: Follow up — the AI remembers the conversation
steps.html:
Within the same conversation, Claude remembers what was said earlier. So you can just say "the second idea" and it knows what you mean.

Send this in the box below its answer.
steps.code: Tell me how to make the second idea, step by step

check.q: Did you get the steps for the second idea it suggested?

steps.title: If the answer is off
steps.html:
• If you sent it in a new chat, Claude doesn't know the earlier part. Send it on the same screen where you see the dinner ideas.
  • If it's still confused, say a bit more, like "how to make the tofu dish you suggested".

steps.title: Hand it a long text to summarize
steps.html: Something AI is especially good at is turning long text into a short summary. Copy the whole practice text below and send it.
steps.code:
Summarize the text below in three lines that a child could understand.

Walking is exercise anyone can do without special equipment. Walking briskly for about 30 minutes a day is known to strengthen the heart and lungs and to help lift your mood. It's best to start with 10 minutes and build up little by little. Wearing comfortable shoes that fit and gently warming up before and after can reduce injuries. Above all, the most important thing is the habit of walking regularly every day.
steps.codeLabel: Copy all of it and send

check.q: Did you get a three-line summary?

faq.q: Where would I use this in real life?
faq.a: Paste in a long notice, a news article or meeting notes and say "summarize in three lines" or "list just the to-dos". Just remove any personal or confidential information first.

steps.title: Not happy? Just ask again
steps.html:
If you don't like the answer, you don't need to start over. Just say how to change it.

This time, ask it to make the summary shorter.
steps.code: Make it shorter, just one line

check.q: Did you get a one-line answer?

faq.q: How do I ask for other changes?
faq.a: Just say it the way you'd talk. e.g. "in a friendlier tone", "more formal", "as a table", "most important first"

phone.html:
When you change topics, start a new chat, so the old conversation doesn't get mixed in.

Tap the pencil or + button at the top of the Claude app, or New chat in the menu (≡) at the top left.

pc.html:
When you change topics, start a new chat, so the old conversation doesn't get mixed in.

Click New chat or the + button at the top left (or in the left menu) of the Claude screen.

check.q: Do you see an empty screen with no conversation?

steps.title: If you can't find the new chat button
steps.html:
The layout changes from time to time. Look for a pencil, +, or New chat. Your earlier chat doesn't disappear; it stays in the chat list in the menu.

It's fine if you can't find it. You're almost done.

steps.title: 🎉 First chat with AI done! What you learned
steps.html:
You've tried all the basics of chatting with AI.

Five things you did today

AskSend what you want to know in plain words
Follow upIn the same chat, it remembers what was said
Hand offPaste a long text and ask for a summary
Ask againJust say what to change, like "shorter" or "as a table"
New chatStart fresh when the topic changes

Remember

  1. Never enter passwords, ID numbers or confidential work
  2. AI can be wrong. Double-check important things

Next step: from 'chat' to 'agent'

What you did today is chat. You ask, read the answer, and if needed copy it yourself into your document.

An AI agent goes one step further: the AI creates and edits files on your computer directly, so it does the copying part too. The best-known example is Claude Code, which needs a computer and a paid plan.
